pr-987: Add a durable cache backed by SQLite (using node:sqlite) that behaves exactly like the existing in-memory cache: one row per identity, a later edit recorded beside the first row, and cursors, gaps and quarantine records read back as written. The database carries a schema version: refuse to open a file written by a newer version, naming the file and both versions, and migrate an older one forward without losing rows. Store each page's rows, quarantine records and new cursor in one transaction so an interrupted process leaves the database at the last complete page. Update the log sync documentation to describe the cache.
pr-990: Add a `vinaya sync` command that copies events from the configured log destination (a folder or a server, using the configured read headers) into the local cache, resumes from where the last run stopped, and prints a summary of pages read, rows stored, duplicates, edits, deletions, gaps, quarantined lines and any lost-event diagnostic from the server. Exit 0 on a completed run, 1 when it failed part way (keeping the progress made) and 2 for a usage or configuration problem, saying which happened. Keep the cache under the repository's runtime directory, add `--rebuild` to delete and refill it, and never write to the destination.
pr-1002: Introduce one confinement interface, independent of the coding agent vendor, that takes a role, its task worktree, its scratch directory and the hosts it may reach, and returns the vendor configuration for that run; make the dispatch path use it for every unattended agent instead of branching on vendor. For Claude, produce Claude Code's own sandbox settings: sandbox enabled, failing if unavailable, no unsandboxed commands or excluded commands, writes allowed only in the worktree and scratch directory, reads denied elsewhere in the home directory, network limited to GitHub and the npm registry, and Read/Edit/Write tool permissions denied outside the allowed directories. It must work on macOS and Linux.
pr-1003: Change how automated code-review and security-review agents get their inputs. Before each review agent starts, the orchestrating driver writes into that agent's read-only input folder the pull request body, the diff of the reviewed head against its base, and the previous round's findings, and names each file in the agent's prompt. Run these review agents with no `gh` tool and no GitHub credential in their environment; each must still produce a valid review result from those files alone. Update the role instructions so an automated review agent reads those inputs and does not call `gh`, while a person running a review at their own terminal keeps the current instructions.
pr-1012: Enrich the review loop's log events with optional fields. A round's review-results event lists one entry per review role the loop held or expected a result from, with the role, its outcome (approve, changes requested, or not reviewed) and its blocking count, and those counts sum to the event's own total. A pause event carries the loop's short pause reason code at every place the loop pauses, never prose. A driver-exited event carries the process exit code when there is one and an error class (the error's code or constructor name, never its message) when it ends on an error. Events also carry the pull request number where one exists.
pr-1060: Fix the sync engine so it decides that a cached row was deleted by its position in the source, never by event time. Report a row as deleted only when its source position lies inside the span of positions the run re-read and the source did not return it. A source whose rows arrive out of event-time order (as events from several machines do) must produce no false deletions; a run that re-reads no earlier positions reports none; a row really removed from inside the re-read span is still reported, with its identity and origin. Update the sync documentation to describe the deletion window as a span of source positions.
pr-1074: Fix the after-turn check that compares protected paths before and after a coding agent's turn. When the orchestrating driver's own tools committed, pushed, opened a pull request or refreshed evidence during the turn, the check must not report a protected-path change or ask the agent to redo its turn. A write to the task's control records made by anything other than a driver tool call must still be reported, for the coding agent and for both review agents. Document in the isolation specification which writes the check attributes to the driver and how.
pr-1077: On Linux, before an unattended Claude Code or Codex run starts, run one trivial command through that agent's real sandbox with the exact settings the run will use; if it fails, refuse to start, quoting the sandbox's own error. When the host sets the environment variable VINAYA_LINUX_SANDBOX_ALLOW_UNIX_SOCKETS=1, a Claude Code run on Linux enables the sandbox's allowAllUnixSockets option, changes no other setting, prints that the Unix-socket filter is off on this host, and still runs the probe first. On macOS, or with the variable unset, never set that option.
pr-1079: When the review loop sends a coding agent back because CI is red, include in its message, for each failed check, the tail of that check's failed job log, redacted and size-capped, so the agent can name the failing test without any GitHub access of its own. Make the agent's read_pull_request tool return the same per-check failure detail for every failed check on the current head. Produce this detail through the one existing log reader the pull-request status read already uses, so redaction, authority stripping and the size cap are identical. Document this in the loop specification.
pr-1086: Add a tool to the driver's dev-tools server, offered to both the Claude Code and the Codex coding agent, that takes one public https URL, fetches it from the driver outside any sandbox, follows redirects, and returns the page's text bounded in size, so the agent can read public documentation with no network allowlist. A fetch counts as reading a required documentation source only when it returned a success status, ended on a public host, returned an allowed text content type and returned content above the same minimum size the existing web-fetch read check uses; the driver writes that read record itself, somewhere the agent cannot write.
pr-1088: When a pre-push hook refuses a push run by the driver, have publish_changes return it to the coding agent as a hook refusal carrying the hook's failing-check and failing-test lines, bounded in size and sanitized, never as a failure outside the hook. When a push fails for any other reason, return the push's own error output, bounded and sanitized, naming the git exit, never only the hook's last progress line. Add a test that drives a real git push through a real failing pre-push hook in a temporary repository and asserts both the classification and that a failing test's name reaches the refusal. Document what a refused push returns in the loop specification.
pr-1091: Stop tests from writing into the real per-repository runtime directory, and clean up what they left behind. The cancel tool must write its loop log under the runtime directory it was given, so an in-process test leaves the real directory unchanged. Add a test guard that fails when any test in the CLI suite creates or changes a file under the real runtime directory. Make the loop's start-up sweep treat a task folder whose Issue GitHub reports as nonexistent as an orphan and remove it, instead of keeping it as unknown on every run.
pr-1093: A fetched documentation page of type text/html should count as reading a required source only when its visible text, after removing script and style elements and tags and collapsing whitespace, reaches the minimum read size; other text content types keep the raw-size rule. An HTML page below the minimum is still returned to the agent, but no read record is written, and the result names the visible-text size as the reason. Expose the visible-text measure as one exported function so other readability checks can reuse it, and document the rule in the loop specification.
pr-1094: Fix the repeat-finding stop in the review loop. Treat two blocking findings as the same finding only when they come from the same review role, name the same file and carry the same normalized description, never because they share a positional identifier. A new blocking finding in a later round that reuses an earlier identifier with a different file or description must not pause the loop as a repeat; a finding that really recurs still does. Every finding observation carries the normalized description fingerprint, built where review output is parsed into observations. Document how the stop identifies a finding in the loop specification.
pr-1100: Before an unattended run starts any agent, prove that the required enforcement controls are active and executable, and refuse the run naming each inactive control and its remedy when any is not. Keep the decision vendor-neutral, with each control proven by its own adapter. The repository's local git hooks are one such control: the hooks path must point at the tracked hook directory and the required hooks must exist there and be executable; a path pointing at a missing directory, or a missing or non-executable required hook, is reported as inactive. Each agent adapter proves its own per-run controls (such as Claude Code's settings and hook scripts) before spawning.
pr-1151: Translate each Claude agent tool call into one plain action: a kind in plain words (reading, searching, editing, creating, removing, running tests, type-checking, git, GitHub, tool request, skill, fetching, delegating) and the subject it acted on, either a repository-relative path or a command shortened to its first word and its target. An edit action carries lines added and removed counted from the call's own old and new text, and a create action carries its line count; neither carries file content. Match each tool result to its call by identifier and record success or failure with the time taken; a failure carries its first error line, shortened and redacted.
pr-1166: Translate a Codex agent's event stream (command runs, file changes, tool calls and messages) into the same plain actions the Claude translator produces: a kind in plain words, the subject, and a result with success or failure and time taken. A command run carries its command's first words and exit status, a file change carries the path and kind of change, and a tool call carries the tool's name; none carries output or file content. An unrecognised event returns no action and never throws. Fed a recorded Codex stream from a real run, the translator must return the expected hand-written action list.
pr-1178: Render every agent line on the terminal and in the loop log file as one short line: time, a status mark, a role label and plain words, for example `10:41:20  ▸ Code review   Reading   apps/cli/src/lib/dispatch.ts`. Use a small fixed set of marks (▸ working, ✓ done, ✕ failed, ◌ waiting, ◆ round), show pause, block and stop as labelled badges rather than symbols, and fall back to >, +, x, ~ and # on terminals without Unicode. Name roles in words so two concurrent review agents are told apart on every line. Show detail lines by default and hide them on request.
pr-1213: Make a task's log show its detail lines by default and hide them with one flag: `vinaya task status --follow` shows detail lines and `--follow --quiet` hides them, and `vinaya task run --quiet` hides them on the live terminal while the log file stays the same either way. Add both flags to the command reference, along with the follow flag that is missing from the status command's row, and document the two `--quiet` flags in the loop specification's agent-line rendering section. Add tests for both modes.
pr-1240: Add a core check named `doc-claims` that evaluates every documentation-claim marker in the tracked doctrine pages under aeg-root and the tracked TypeScript and Markdown files under apps and packages, reports as an error each marker that parses as neither supported form and each binding whose cited text the cited file no longer contains, and passes with the verified binding count noted when there are none. Register it with full scope so `vinaya check --all` runs it in the pre-push hook, in CI and through the run_checks tool, while the pre-commit hook skips it. Make the default branch pass by rebinding the markers that fail today.
pr-1249: Bring the rendered task instructions and the two templates in line with what the orchestration tools actually do. Remove any instruction a tool refuses or already performs: pasting the task instructions into the pull request body, including a token report, confirming dispatch readiness by hand, and running the documentation gate by hand before opening. State one publication rule: publish once when every part is done, then open the pull request; publish again only to answer review findings or a red gate. Update the task instruction template and the pull request report template to match, turning the checkbox placeholder into a fenced command block.
pr-1268: Clean up the planning role's documentation so it claims only enforcement that actually runs. Rewrite the sentences about the project registry, conflict completeness, editing dependency edges and milestones so each describes the real refusal, warning location, Issue edit command or automatic milestone attachment. Remove every rule sentence that a check, gate or tool already enforces, and every rule about a retired mechanism (topology files, the `#TBD` placeholder, the deprecated dispatch command, an unused clarification marker). Make its template pass the Issue gate.
pr-1271: Make the review prompt that the driver renders state, as driver text, which severities block under the effective review policy for that role, read from the policy the manifest digest already binds and never typed by hand, so the review agent learns the threshold from the same source used to derive its result. Remove from the code-review and security role documentation every sentence that names its own blocking threshold, replacing it with a reference to the repository's policy, and note that a documentation sentence without a binding marker is at most a minor finding since the binding check now runs on every push.
pr-1273: Add one command that continues a paused task whose agent asked to widen the set of files it may change: `vinaya task run <tranche> <n>` with a new flag taking the requested globs and a `--reason <text>` flag (plus an `--issue <n>` form). In order it supersedes the frozen task instructions with the widened file set, runs the write gate over the new body, and starts the run; it refuses before any step when the pause is not a widen request, when a driver is still alive for the task, or when the widened body fails the gate, naming the exact gap. A pause asking to widen names this command, with the requested globs, among its next actions, and the resume tool refuses such a pause naming the same command.
pr-1277: Update the front-door skill, the role-routing skill, the state machine and the model documents under the doctrine root so none presents a retired mechanism as live: the tranche topology file, the `aeg-root/tranches/` directory and the `aeg-project/` state directory may appear only in the tranche model's own retirement section. Make the `retired-vocabulary` check recognise those three as retired, exempt only that retirement section by file, and block: a finding exits 1 and fails `check --all`, and the default branch passes after the sweep. Make the front door's description, its list of what the repository holds and its reading order name what exists today.
pr-1299: Add the code-and-review evaluation program specification to the repository as an exact byte-for-byte mirror of its revision 11 body, assembled from its source chunks in their given order, UTF-8 with LF line endings and nothing added, so its SHA-256 equals the pinned digest. Beside it, add a provenance manifest recording the source URL, source document ID, revision 11, retrieval date, each source chunk ID in order with its byte count and SHA-256, the total byte count, the complete SHA-256, and a map from each document the mirror names by title to its repository path.
pr-1312: Add a registry shard that carries every row of the evaluation program's fault-and-attack matrix, fifty-eight rows, each with the ten required fields, its source document, revision and section, its owning suite, its layers, its expected typed outcome and its declared cutover outcome. Its completeness check must derive the row set by parsing the fault-and-attack table in the repository's mirror of the specification, and fail when a row is missing, extra, differs from the table in suite, layer, expected outcome or cutover outcome, or has an empty field. Each row whose cutover outcome is "must pass" states that no known-failure entry is admitted for it.
pr-1320: Add one global exit check that aggregates every registry shard and reports, by component kind, the components covered, the empty fields and the unmapped components. It passes only when the complete kind set read from the registry's COMPONENT_KINDS is present, every expected shard is present, the cutover gates number seventeen, the fault-and-attack rows number fifty-eight, every catalog module is named by at least one component, and the empty-field and unmapped counts are both zero; otherwise it fails naming the gap.
